newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BRAVE BARSBY CENTURY EXTENDS QUEENSLAND LEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BRAVE BARSBY CENTURY EXTENDS QUEENSLAND LEAD.

text.p: Opening batsman Trevor Barsby defied illness on Sunday to score a century as Queensland tightened their grip on Western Australia on the third day of the Sheffield Shield final.
Barsby, playing in his 100th and last Shield match, had an upset stomach before taking the field, where he proceeded to spend over five hours at the crease in scoring 111.
His innings allowed Queensland to reach 259 for six at the close at the WACA ground for an overall lead of 414.

Western Australia's first innings earlier lasted just another seven balls after the hosts resumed at 164 for nine. Former Australia pace bowler bowler Michael Kasprowicz snared tail-ender Bret Mulder cheaply for pre-match favourites Western Australia to be all out for 165.
Queensland must win the five-day match to capture the Shield title while Western Australia need only avoid defeat because of their higher finish on the table at the end of the regular season.
Barsby's dismissal by pace bowler Matthew Garnaut sparked a mini-collapse, with the big-hitting Andrew Symonds run out for 30 on the next ball and fellow all-rounder Geoff Foley then out for two.
Wade Seccombe was six not out and tail-ender Paul Jackson unbeaten on 10 at the close.

Barsby, 33, raced to his half century in 99 minutes before lunch but was more circumspect after the interval and fought illness and fatigue while spending over three hours to add another 50 and bring up his century.
He shared a partnership of 131 for the third wicket with captain Stuart Law.
Law, who was named on Sunday to join the Australia squad for their forthcoming limited overs series in South Africa, made 72.
